Navi · Accessible indoor navigation

Indoor navigation.
Led by voice.

A navigation concept for blind and low-vision users. Confirm where you are, say where you want to go, and hear the next step through mapped indoor spaces.

01 / The prototype

Four states. One conversation.

Select a screen to explore what Navi would say and do at that point in a trip.

01 / Listening

“Where would you like to go?”

Activate Navi with the configured supported shortcut, say a destination, and confirm the building, floor, and room before a route is chosen.

02 / Guiding

“Stop, then turn left.”

Follow spoken distance, stop, and turn instructions along the confirmed route. The proposed experience supports fastest, familiar, and avoid-stairs preferences where eligible routes exist.

03 / Paused

“Please clear the camera.”

Guidance pauses when the camera view becomes unclear. Correct the view, then say resume; Navi rechecks camera and location before continuing.

04 / Arrived

“You’ve arrived.”

Navi announces arrival when the confirmed location matches the mapped destination entrance. Say stop to end the navigation session.

Concept screens from the Team 2 presentation. These illustrate the planned app experience.

01 / Confirm

Step 1 of 6 · Entrance

Read the complete journey
AS-IS and TO-BE storyboard from the project presentation
StageAS-ISTO-BE
1. EntranceThe user enters an unfamiliar mapped building and cannot confirm the starting point.Double press. Confirm the lobby location and “Library, floor 2.”
2. Route choiceSimilar corridors make the turn toward the library uncertain.Choose avoid-stairs. Hear the next turn on the eligible elevator route.
3. ObstructionA cart blocks the corridor. The user stops and reassesses with a cane.“Stop. A cart is ahead.” Pause until the path clears or a detour is confirmed.
4. RecoveryThe user asks staff where to find the elevator and library floor.If the view fails: “Pause. Clear and face the camera forward.” Say resume after checks pass.
5. Floor changeAfter the elevator trip, the user must establish the new floor and heading.At the elevator exit, confirm floor 2 and heading before another turn.
6. ArrivalStaff help identify the library entrance. Arrival depends on local assistance.Match the mapped library entrance and announce arrival. Say stop.

Illustrative storyboard from our presentation; this is a proposed experience, not a recorded user trial.

03 / Voice interaction

Keep the conversation
in your control.

The proposed experience supports short voice commands throughout a trip. Select one to see the intended response.

Navi’s intended response

Directional guidance pauses until the user resumes or ends the trip.

Confirm before routing.
Read back the destination and confirm the starting location.
Pause when inputs fail.
Explain the camera or location problem before resuming guidance.
Respect route preferences.
Offer eligible routes with fastest, familiar, or avoid-stairs choices.
